concerns.concern: Joule heating at 4 mA (about 6–8 mW in a 5×5 µm region) changes lattice parameters and the Bragg peak directly. The 'immediate erasure' at switching may therefore be a trivial strain/temperature effect rather than erased domain memory. Mean-diffraction observables (peak position, width, intensity, M1/R ratio) versus time are not reported.
concerns.quote: The "immediate erasure" at switching (Fig. 3b) is therefore expected trivially from strain/temperature changes.

concerns.concern: The apparent 'learning' could come from the sample holder and contacts reaching a periodic thermal steady state, which reduces sample drift and so raises speckle correlation. Controls such as Off-state gating, sub-threshold cycling, a reference reflection and retraining after rest are needed.
concerns.quote: Its slowdown as the setup equilibrates would raise ΔG with no material "learning".

concerns.concern: The focused X-ray beam delivers a large cumulative dose and may itself drive the dynamics through vacancy creation, heating or photo-metallization. No dose-rate, attenuated-beam or fresh-spot controls are shown, so the τ values and the sub-threshold decorrelation cannot be called intrinsic.
concerns.quote: No dose-rate dependence, attenuated-beam control, or fresh-spot comparison is shown.

concerns.concern: The claim that switching becomes deterministic, and that sub-threshold currents restore stochasticity, is never checked electrically. No per-cycle threshold, delay, resistance or I–V statistics are shown, and the XPCS correlation is only a proxy.
concerns.quote: Yet no electrical statistics are shown versus cycle number

concerns.concern: The train–erase–retrain sequence is never performed. Erasure was measured only on an untrained state, so the in-device learning and erasure claim is an extrapolation.
concerns.quote: The key neuromorphic claim is therefore an extrapolation, not an observation.

concerns.concern: Fitted τ values are far longer than the measurement windows. β and τ are therefore strongly covariant and β is poorly constrained, as shown by the large error bars and scatter.
concerns.quote: In this regime, β and τ are strongly covariant and β is poorly constrained.

concerns.concern: A single τ is imposed for all aging times while β varies freely, so any real aging of τ is forced into β. The β 'transition' may be a fitting artefact; free τ(t_age) fits, residuals, χ² and covariances are needed.
concerns.quote: The β(t_age) "transition" may thus be a fitting artefact.

concerns.concern: The sub-threshold current, which forms no filament, shows the same β transition. This contradicts the claim that electrical switching induces jamming and suggests the transition is generic to the measurement or its history.
concerns.quote: This conflicts with the statement that "electrical switching induces a jamming transition".

concerns.concern: Calling the result a jamming transition is not justified. The paper shows no q-dependence of τ (diffusive vs ballistic), no dynamic-heterogeneity measures, no control parameter, and no 1/q² scaling supporting the 'liquid-like' β=1 assignment.
concerns.quote: Calling this a "jamming transition" rather than a crossover in decorrelation shape is therefore not justified.

concerns.concern: The causal link between jamming and learning rests only on coincident ~10³ s timescales. The two were measured under different protocols (constant current vs on/off cycling), and that timescale also matches setup thermalization.
concerns.quote: The only connection drawn is that both occur on ~10³ s timescales

concerns.concern: Each key experiment seems to be a single run on a single device. Reproducibility of the learning curve across runs and devices is not established, and the pristine-device data supporting generality are only in the SI.
concerns.quote: Each key experiment appears to be a single run on a single device.

concerns.concern: The beam spot is larger than the 5×5 µm channel and also illuminates film near the electrodes, which heat and expand. The fraction of signal from the filament region is not estimated.
concerns.quote: The fraction of the signal coming from the filament region is not estimated, so it is unclear what the correlation actually reports.

concerns.concern: The Joule-heating/Arrhenius explanation is internally inconsistent. The 4 mA On-state τ is slower than the 298 K no-current τ even though the device should be hotter, and this is not discussed.
concerns.quote: This contradicts thermally activated acceleration and is not discussed.

concerns.concern: The activation energy seems to come from only two or three temperatures. One of them (340 K) lies inside the MIT, where the dynamics are non-stationary and a stationary τ is ill-defined.
concerns.quote: E_a = 230 ± 70 meV appears to come from very few temperatures, possibly only two or three in the inset.

concerns.concern: Comparing E_a/k_B to the melting temperature conflates a barrier height with a thermodynamic transition temperature. It has no clear physical basis for M1/R domain-wall motion.
concerns.quote: conflates a barrier height with a thermodynamic transition temperature

concerns.concern: The shear-thickening analogy is unsupported. It rests on one point with 75% uncertainty, and shear-thickening concerns viscosity versus drive rate, not delay to a jammed state.
concerns.quote: The trend "larger current → slower jamming" rests on one point with 75% uncertainty.

concerns.concern: The M1 (200) and R (011) reflections have nearly identical d-spacings. The paper does not explain whether both are captured, how their contributions are separated, or which phase produces the speckle.
concerns.quote: The M1 (200) and R (011) reflections are very close in d-spacing (~2.42 Å).

concerns.concern: The 20 nm domain size from the peak width may be dominated by film thickness, mosaicity, strain gradients or instrumental resolution. The direction of Q_FWHM is not given.
concerns.quote: R_d = 2π/Q_FWHM = 20 nm may be dominated by film thickness (45 nm), mosaicity, strain gradients or instrumental resolution

concerns.concern: The abstract and conclusions present deterministic switching, erasure that recovers stochasticity, and in-device learning as findings. They should be stated as hypotheses unless directly demonstrated.
concerns.quote: Adjust the abstract and conclusions so that "deterministic switching", "erasure recovering stochasticity" and "in-device learning" are stated as hypotheses

concerns.concern: Persistent domains and ramp-reversal and subthreshold memory in VO₂ are already established. Novelty therefore rests on the method and on the jamming interpretation, which are the least supported parts.
concerns.quote: These are exactly the elements that currently need the strongest support.

concerns.concern: β > 1 is a compressed exponent, not a 'stretching' exponent as written. The relevant soft-matter literature should be cited correctly.
concerns.quote: β > 1 is a *compressed* exponent, not a "stretching" exponent as written.

concerns.concern: The 'domain speeds' promised in the text are never reported.
concerns.quote: The "domain speeds" promised in the text are never reported.

concerns.concern: The room-temperature stability limit is given as 8000 ± 3000 s in the text but 81000 ± 3000 s in Fig. 2c.
concerns.quote: The room-temperature limit is given as "8000 ± 3000 s" in the text but τ = 81000 ± 3000 s in Fig. 2c.

concerns.concern: The constant-current On-state τ is 150000 ± 50000 s in the text but 160000 ± 50000 s in Fig. 3h.
concerns.quote: The constant-current On-state τ is "150000 ± 50000 s" in the text but 160000 ± 50000 s in Fig. 3h.

concerns.concern: The sub-threshold current is 0.26 mA in Fig. 3 but 0.27 mA in Fig. 4.
concerns.quote: The sub-threshold current is 0.26 mA in Fig. 3 but 0.27 mA in Fig. 4.

concerns.concern: The cycle timing (3 s on and off, 1 s acquisition) does not obviously match about 1800 cycles in about 5000 s.
concerns.quote: The cycle timing ("on and off for 3 s", 1 s acquisition) does not obviously match ~1800 cycles in ~5000 s.

concerns.concern: The normalization of ΔG(n,n+1) to the range [0,1] is not defined.
concerns.quote: The normalization of ΔG(n,n+1) to [0,1] is not defined.

concerns.concern: The irradiation is described as a central 5×5 µm region in the main text but as global in Methods.
concerns.quote: Irradiation is described as a "central 5×5 µm region" in the main text but "globally irradiated" in Methods.

concerns.concern: The text refers to an orange-data inset in Fig. 3i that does not exist.
concerns.quote: The text refers to an "inset (orange data)" in Fig. 3i that does not exist.

concerns.concern: Real-space imaging before and after training (nanodiffraction or dark-field X-ray microscopy) would help verify a persistent filament or domain template.
concerns.quote: complement with real-space imaging (nanodiffraction or dark-field X-ray microscopy) before and after training
